how many requests marked closed were ver.question: How many requests marked closed were verified fixed?

how many requests marked closed were ver.name: query_metric
how many requests marked closed were ver.sql:
with grouped as (
    select
        sum(case when (NOT COALESCE(outcome_group, '') IN ('neutral', 'handed_off')) and (outcome_group = 'fixed') then n_requests else 0 end) as numerator,
        sum(case when (NOT COALESCE(outcome_group, '') IN ('neutral', 'handed_off')) then n_requests else 0 end) as denominator
    from mart_outcomes_monthly
    where ("is_closed" in (?)) and (created_month between ? and ?) and (era = 'current')
)
select *, numerator / nullif(denominator, 0) as value_
from grouped

how many requests marked closed were ver.name: query_metric

with grouped as (
    select
        sum(case when (NOT COALESCE(outcome_group, '') IN ('neutral', 'handed_off')) and (is_closed AND COALESCE(outcome_group, '') <> 'fixed') then n_requests else 0 end) as n
    from mart_outcomes_monthly
    where (created_month between ? and ?) and (era = 'current')
)
select *, n as value_
from grouped

answer.answer_markdown: Among requests marked closed, **1,282,411 of 1,813,376 (70.7%)** were verified fixed, meaning their resolution code says work was done or already resolved. This covers current-era requests created March 2025 to July 2026. About **530,965** requests were marked closed in the fix-rate base without a code saying the problem was fixed.

Many unverified closes carry generic codes, so they mean 'not recorded as fixed', not 'not fixed'.

answer.answer_markdown:
Three codes carry most of the gap. For March 2025 to July 2026, the **closed_fixed_gap_pp is 25.7 percentage points**. That means 87.8% of requests in the base were closed and 62.1% were verified fixed. The requests closed without a fix code, by resolution code:

- **QC-Item Not Out: 317,748**. This is the largest by far. It is mapped to `not_found`, meaning the item wasn't put out for pickup. That can be a legitimate outcome, but it isn't a fix.
- **C-Closed: 105,644**. This is a generic closure code.
- **1004-Closed: 52,198**. This is also generic.
- Much smaller: 1003-Referral to External Department (**14,957**), IWO-Issued Work Orders to Resolve (6,042), MNT-Maintenance to Be Performed (4,624), UTM-Unable to Make (3,994) and NCPP-Not at Curb / On Private Property (3,944).
- Closed with no code at all: 1,832.

So one specific code (item not out) and two generic closure codes account for most of the gap. I didn't calculate each code's percentage share of the gap, because the tools gave me counts only.
caveats: Current era only, creation months 2025-03 to 2026-07. Legacy data has no resolution codes.
Generic codes such as C-Closed and 1004-Closed mean "not recorded as fixed", not "not fixed". QC-Item Not Out can be a legitimate outcome.
Code counts are listed for the top 12 codes only; I didn't compute each code's share of the gap.

did graffiti requests close faster or sl.question: Did graffiti requests close faster or slower after the March 2025 relaunch?

did graffiti requests close faster or sl.name: query_metric
did graffiti requests close faster or sl.sql:
with grouped as (
    select
        "period" as period,
        sum(case when (NOT FALSE) then n_closed_within_30d else 0 end) as numerator,
        sum(case when (NOT FALSE) then case when cross_era_comparison <> 'volume_only' then n_requests end else 0 end) as denominator
    from mart_cutover_periods
    where ("unified_category" in (?))
    group by period
)
select *, numerator / nullif(denominator, 0) as value_
from grouped
order by period

    select
        "period" as period,
        sum(case when (NOT FALSE) then n_closed_within_7d else 0 end) as numerator,
        sum(case when (NOT FALSE) then case when cross_era_comparison <> 'volume_only' then n_requests end else 0 end) as denominator
    from mart_cutover_periods
    where ("unified_category" in (?))
    group by period

answer.answer_markdown:
Resident-reported graffiti requests were closed **slower** after the relaunch, on both speed measures. Here, "before" is Feb 2024 to Feb 2025 (legacy system) and "after" is Sep 2025 to Aug 2026 (current system).

- **Closed within 7 days:** **66.4%** before, **57.2%** after.
- **Closed within 30 days:** **74.4%** before, **65.1%** after.

Both rates count requests that never closed, so they aren't distorted by requests still open. The data shows what changed and when. It doesn't show why.
caveats: Covers resident-reported graffiti only. Crew self-reports are excluded, and the overlap months (Apr-Aug 2025) are left out.
The two systems record status differently, so this compares closure behavior and not whether the graffiti was actually removed.

order by value_ desc nulls last, cd

answer.answer_markdown: Among council districts, **CD 13** has the biggest gap at **30.8 percentage points**. Next are **CD 6** (**29.3**) and **CD 4** (**29.1**). The gap is the share of all requests in the fix-rate base that were marked closed without a code saying the work was done. The smallest gaps are **CD 8** (**19.6**) and **CD 1** (**20.5**). Requests with no district have a gap of **36.0**, but that is a small group of 7,227 requests. The window is current-era requests created March 2025 to July 2026.
caveats: Only current-era data has resolution codes, so this can't be shown for the legacy system.
A gap means 'not recorded as fixed', not 'not fixed'. Many categories close with generic codes, and the district gaps reflect each district's mix of request types.
Requests with no district (null cd) are listed separately and are not a council district.
